# Conservative truncation across cities (generated by market/conservative_summary.py; do not edit by hand)

Frozen rule from docs/CONSERVATIVE_TRUNCATION.md: margin = nearest-rank 99th percentile of positive training sensor-minus-official errors, rounded up to 0.5F; 80% minute coverage; 5-minute feed delay; common b and fee from forecast-only training PnL. Each city fits its own margin. Test days Jun 1 - Aug 13, 2026, coverage-qualified.

Not evaluable under the frozen coverage rule (fewer than 20 training days with 80% of minutes present): DCA.

## Caveats

- NYC motivated the rule and CHI was a registered replication; LAX, AUS and MSP were run afterwards with the rule unchanged. Unguarded results for every city had been seen before.
- With 20-45 training days the 99th percentile is the largest training error, so a single bad reading sets the margin. In LAX a 120F reading on a 68F day (May 24) gives a 52F margin, which switches truncation off; the frozen rule has no plausibility filter and we did not add one after seeing this.
- Counterfactual replay; hypothetical maker fee; feed delay is a proxy.
